/workspace/agenticgen_uniguide_flowr_202.mechanism_uncertainty: The coordinate correction is delta = -dt * S * ((1-t+1e-6)/t + gamma(t)) * grad_x L(endpoint(x,t), detached_target), with the endpoint-to-current Jacobian retained across the whole valid ligand while target, assignment, parameters and self-conditioning stay fixed during the VJP. Scale, unit conversion, loss reduction and the model Jacobian therefore act jointly: S is the same constant across all four windows of R05/increase, yet measured increment rms falls from 0.393059 A (window 1) to 0.130127, 0.021991 and 0.013481 A, so equal S demonstrably does not imply equal displacement per window or per teacher. The R04/increase -> R05/increase pair isolates one window and shows a sqrt(2) coefficient increase (coefficient_first -4.133096 -> -5.845080) producing only a 1.39x increment-rms increase and a 0.0045 C change, i.e. coefficient scaling is not proportional to geometric effect. Because the endpoint proxy in the changed window rose (0.153616 -> 0.174819) while final C fell, a smaller endpoint proxy and a better final C are not interchangeable, and a rising window loss alone cannot establish under-dosing; equally, a larger lambda could worsen final geometry despite reducing the endpoint proxy, which was not observed here but is not excluded at this effect size. Assignment switches are discontinuities, not evidence of improved binding; the switch mean in the changed window is 0.000148, so switching is not the driver of the observed change, but the first window's 0.055694 switches and 4.455268 guidance/native ratio remain an unresolved confounder shared by all increase runs. Finally, C_se 0.031-0.035 is a marginal standard error, and all cited differences (dC 0.004465, dgap 0.003231, dC 0.037806 vs R0) are exploratory, not significance claims.
